title: NextWave's priority is a mechanical v2 rescore, so its open-source screen has not run
content:
NextWave Consulting's priority is derived, not scored. The row was carried over from the v2 ranking and rescored mechanically on two inputs only — size and slot occupancy — and the record says so explicitly, together with the instruction to run the OSS-portfolio screen before acting. Its priority 2 therefore means the thesis question is open, not that the lead has been qualified.

The gap matters because the criteria that actually decide the interesting cases are the ones missing. Size and slot occupancy are mechanical: headcount and which platform is carried. Open-source posture, sovereignty alignment and whether the firm's portfolio suggests it would carry client-owned infrastructure all require reading the firm, and none of that has been done here. What is on file is an Appian practice — including an Appian EMEA Innovation Award — and v2 verticals of banking and risk.

Recorded as a data-quality note rather than an assessment, this is a reminder that the workbook mixes two kinds of row: judged and rescored. The rescored ones look identical in the priority column and carry much less evidence, so any batch action taken on priority alone will treat them as equivalent when they are not.
